messages:
Kevin L: Quick experiment summary — compared INT8-KV vs FP8-KV on pythia-12b (1024 ctx, beam decode, batch 16). INT8 reduces KV memory (~38%) but p95/p99 latency increased; decode-quality drift shows up on long tails.
Maria S: Can you paste the exact repro command?
Kevin L: `./run_infer --model pythia-12b --kv-quant int8 --calib linear --batch 16 --max-len 1024 --decode beam` — ran 3 seeds, stable-ish.
infra-bot: profiling artifact uploaded: s3://redwood-perf/1805123456/kv-int8-fp8-run.tar.gz
Jordan P: Share p50/p95/p99 and mem numbers?
Kevin L: summary numbers (median across runs): p50: 52ms (fp32-kv baseline 48ms), p95: 180ms (baseline 160ms), p99: 340ms (baseline 300ms). KV mem per-shard: baseline 1.9GB -> INT8 1.2GB, FP8 1.35GB.
Samir: so INT8 is best for footprint but worse on tails — suggests extra kernel conversions or fallback paths.
Maria S: any automated quality metrics? ppl/repitition?
Kevin L: ppl on held-out eval: baseline 3.7, FP8: 3.75, INT8: 3.9. Quality delta concentrated after ~800 tokens; also ~6% increase in long exact-repeat segments (>8 tokens) for INT8.
Jordan P: did the kernel selector pick different kernels for INT8? traces?
Kevin L: yes — saw fallback to generic int8 GEMM at larger seq lengths. Trace excerpt:
```
select_kernel: q8_gemm_fast if seq<=512 && bs<=32 else q8_gemm_generic
kernel_launches: fast: 1200, generic: 400
observed_extra_syncs: 24
```
Maria S: hmm. maybe our batching heuristic causes microbatch shapes that push the selector into slow path. Could tweak continuous-batching thresholds.
Samir: I tried forcing smaller microbatches to keep seq<=512 and that reduced p95 by ~8% but increased overall GPU utilization and marginally reduced throughput. Tradeoff surface is tight.
Jordan P: for FP8, what did calibration look like? per-layer linear vs per-channel?
Kevin L: FP8 with per-layer linear calibration gave best latency/quality balance. Per-channel barely helped quality but added ~6% extra calibr time and slightly more memory during warmup.
Maria S: any quick mitigation we can roll? e.g., fallback to FP8 for long-context requests or a hybrid KV policy?
Kevin L: two pragmatic options: (A) default to FP8-KV for requests > 700 tokens; (B) keep INT8-KV but force microbatching config to maintain fast-kernel shapes. Option A simpler to implement as a routing rule.
Jordan P: propose experiments to run tomorrow: 1) INT8 + tuned microbatch=8 + per-layer calib; 2) FP8 + kernel config tweak + stash-convert-on-KV-update to avoid conversions during decode. Compare p95/p99 and ppl at 1k tokens.
Kevin L: I ran #1 locally — p95 down to 165ms, p99 310ms, ppl 3.88. Better but still not as good as FP8 quality numbers. Pushing artifacts + recipe to perf board.
Maria S: TL;DR for product: FP8 gives best quality/latency balance; INT8 wins on memory but needs careful batching/kernel work to avoid tail regressions.
Samir: adding to action items: (1) kernel-selector thresholds review, (2) microbatching autotuner test, (3) routing rule experiment for long-context fallback.
Jordan P: also set an alert for decode-quality regressions on long-context evals (>=1k tokens) so we catch drift early.
Kevin L: thanks — I'll attach the reproducible notebook and job configs to the artifact.
infra-bot: artifact published: https://artifacts.redwood.ai/kvquant/1805123456
